title: Independent projectile directions
target: Explain why horizontal and vertical projectile motion share time but evolve differently.
criteria: Identify horizontal and vertical velocity components.
Use the same elapsed time for both axes.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A projectile moves with vx = 5 m/s and vy = −2 m/s, with upward positive. Which description is correct?
cpa.guide: The components specify simultaneous horizontal and vertical motion.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: In ideal projectile motion without air resistance, which acceleration components apply?
options: ax = 0; ay = −g when upward is positive.
Both point along the current velocity.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A projectile travels horizontally at 7 m/s for a flight lasting 1.5 s. What horizontal displacement results?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two horizontal launches from the same height have speeds 3 and 9 m/s. Ignore air resistance. Compare times to the same lower landing level.
options: The faster launch takes one-third as long.
The faster launch takes three times as long.
Neither can fall while moving horizontally.
cpa.guide: Vertical initial velocity and vertical displacement are identical, so flight times match.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Which assumption allows horizontal velocity to remain constant after launch?
options: Negligible horizontal force, including air resistance.
cpa.guide: Zero horizontal net force gives zero horizontal acceleration.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Strong air resistance slows a real projectile horizontally. What must change in the ideal model?
options: Continue using constant vx without qualification.
Allow horizontal velocity to vary with time.
Remove elapsed time from both axes.
Set vertical acceleration to zero automatically.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
